structure.proved_step: LEMMA B (unit-clause pinning = contraction, restricted form without auxiliary variables). Let the instance be c_i=(a_i,b_i), i in [m], and fix a unit constraint u with a_u = e_j, b_u = c (x_j = c). Let M be the binary matroid on {v_i : i != u} plus e, and let M/U be the contraction by U = v_u. Substituting x_j = c gives the system c'_i = (a'_i, b'_i) on n-1 variables, with a'_i = a_i restricted to coordinates != j and b'_i = b_i + a_{ij} c. Then the MUS clutter of the substituted system equals the port of M/U at e (as subsets of [m] minus u). Proof: phi(a,b) = (a restricted to coordinates != j, b + a_j c) is GF(2)-linear with kernel span{U}, since phi(e_j,c)=0 and phi(a,b)=0 forces a=t e_j, b=t c. Hence r_{M/U}(X) = r(X cup U) - r(U) = rank of phi(X), so M/U is the binary matroid of phi(v_i) plus phi(e) = e'. Lemma A applied to the substituted system finishes the proof. Hence the MUS clutter of the restriction x_j=c is the port of a minor (a contraction) of the original matroid, so port-preservation holds for unit-clause gadgets without auxiliary variables.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA C (private-auxiliary gadgets, affine GF(2) case). Setting: original system with constraints c_i=(a_i,b_i), i in [m], H_i = {x in GF(2)^n : a_i.x=b_i}. For each i take a gadget E_i = a finite set of affine equations over (x, z_i), where z_i are auxiliaries PRIVATE to i (disjoint across i), such that proj_x sol(E_i) = H_i. Gadget system G = disjoint union of E_i, each equation owned by i. Claims: (i) G consistent iff original consistent; more generally for any owner set P, G|_P consistent iff original restricted to P consistent. (ii) For any S in G, let S_i = S cap E_i and P_i = proj_x sol(S_i). Then S is consistent iff no S_i is internally inconsistent and the intersection of the P_i is nonempty (private aux => lifts are independent). (iii) If a_i != 0 or b_i = 0 then P_i in {H_i, whole space, empty}, since an affine subspace containing a hyperplane is the hyperplane or everything. Internal inconsistency of S_i forces E_i inconsistent, i.e. a_i=0, b_i=1. (iv) Pushforward: if S is an MUS of G and no S_i is internally inconsistent, the owner set Q={i: P_i = H_i} is an original MUS. Proof: Q is inconsistent since the intersection of H_i over Q is empty. If Q' is a proper inconsistent subset of Q, pick j in Q minus Q'; deleting S_j makes the remaining intersection a subset of the intersection over Q', hence empty, so S is not minimal. Also owners with P_i = whole contribute no equations to an MUS, so S = union of S_j over j in Q. (v) Every original MUS M is realized: for each j in M choose a minimal T_j in E_j with proj = H_j; then union T_j is an MUS of G with owner set M. Scope: all gadget auxiliaries private to one constraint, affine (GF(2)-linear) gadgets only. Shared auxiliaries across constraints are NOT covered; G0001 stays open for that case. Lemma C does not claim anything about general Post-lattice languages.

structure.refuted_approach: Claim (iv) of S0003 (MUS pushforward: owner set Q={i: P_i=H_i} of a G-MUS is an original MUS) does NOT extend to non-affine private gadgets. Hand-checked counterexample on domain {0,1,2,3} with one private aux bit per gadget (relations as bitmasks over 8 values, projected by p&3): H0={0,2,3} from E0=[149,133], H1={1} from E1=[26,99], H2={1,3} from E2=[138]. The G-MUS S uses one equation per gadget: P0=H0, P1=proj([99])={0,1,2} strictly containing H1, P2=H2. The intersection of all P_i is empty and every single deletion leaves it nonempty, so S is a G-MUS with no internally inconsistent part. The filtered owner set Q={0,2} has H0∩H2={3} nonempty, so Q is consistent and cannot be an original MUS. Mechanism: the projection of a SUBSET of a gadget always contains H_i; the affine proof uses (iii) (a hyperplane-containing subspace is H_i or the whole space), which fails for general relations. Scope: this refutes the extension only; S0003 itself (affine case) is unaffected.

structure.evidence: the constant-value condition on gadget functions on H_Q guarantees that the pushforward of any inconsistent subset corresponds to an original MUS, establishing the equivalence of MUS families.
structure.lemma: For a gadget system G where each gadget i is defined by the affine relation z_i = g_i·x + h_i (mod 2) with projection onto X = {x | a_i·x = b_i}, let Q ⊆ [m] be any subset such that H_Q = ⋂_{i∈Q} H_i ≠ ∅. If for every i∈Q and every x∈H_Q the values g_i·x + h_i are constant (i.e., there exists c_Q ∈ {0,1} with g_i·x + h_i = c_Q for all i∈Q and all x∈H_Q), then the family of minimal inconsistent subsets (MUS) of G equals the family of minimal inconsistent subsets of the original constraint system {a_i·x = b_i}_{i∈[m]}, so the MUS clutter of G equals the MUS clutter of the original system.

structure.lemma: SPECIAL CASE OF G0001 (shared auxiliaries). Author model: claude-haiku-5-5, so no SURVIVED_REVIEW is possible from this session; a reviewer from another model family is needed. Setting: x in {0,1}^n; gadgets E_i with projections H_i = proj_x(sol(E_i)); each E_i has private auxiliaries (pairwise disjoint across i) and shared auxiliaries Z_i. Hypotheses: (FUNC) for each i and each x in H_i, the Z_i-values of any solution of E_i over x are unique; write f_i(x). (AGREE) for all i, j and x in H_i intersect H_j, f_i(x) and f_j(x) agree on Z_i intersect Z_j. Claim: for every owner set P, G|_P (the union of E_i for i in P) is consistent iff the intersection of H_i over i in P is nonempty. Proof. Soundness (any shared auxiliaries): a solution (x,z) of G|_P gives x in H_i for every i in P, so x lies in the intersection. Completeness: take x in the intersection; define Z-values by f_i(x), well defined on all of Z by AGREE; for each i take a private witness of E_i at x (private sets are disjoint, so witnesses combine); by FUNC the Z_i-values of that witness equal f_i(x), so each E_i is satisfied; hence G|_P is consistent. Scope: covers shared auxiliaries that are functions of x in each gadget (Tseitin-style definitions, XOR chains). Does NOT close G0001 for general shared auxiliaries, where FUNC fails. Sanity check against cm-cbb126d3f0404136: H1 and H2 meet at (0,1), but E1 forces z=0 and E2 forces z=1 there, so AGREE fails, consistent with the lemma. Closes: none (special case only; G0001 stays open).

structure.proved_step: Decoupling lemma for a shared existential bit. Setting: finite X; gadgets G_i subset of X x {0,1}; owner projection C_i = {x : exists z, (x,z) in G_i}; for T a set of gadget indices, shared(T) = {x : exists z, for all i in T, (x,z) in G_i} and owner(T) = intersection over i in T of C_i. Hypothesis (forced constants): for each i there is c_i in {0,1} with (x,z) in G_i implies z = c_i. Claim: if all c_i with i in T are equal to c, then shared(T) = owner(T); otherwise shared(T) is empty. Proof: if all c_i = c on T, then (x,z) in G_i forces z = c, so shared(T) = {x : (x,c) in G_i for all i in T}; and (x,c) in G_i iff x in C_i, because z is forced to c whenever x is in C_i. Hence shared(T) = owner(T). If c_i differ on T, no single z satisfies all gadgets in T, so shared(T) is empty. Scope: this is exact only for forced-constant gadgets, where the shared bit is already a constant and the formalization reduces to private gadgets with fixed values. It does NOT close G0001, which concerns shared bits not forced to a constant. Refutation of the determined-z repair (z = f_i(x) on each gadget): X = {x0,x1}, G_1 = {(x,z): z = [x = x1]}, G_2 = {(x,z): z = [x = x0]}, both with x-domain {x0,x1}. Owner: C_1 and C_2 both equal {x0,x1}, so owner({1,2}) is nonempty. Shared: z would need [x=x1] = [x=x0] for some x, which never holds, so shared({1,2}) is empty. Thus z is determined by x on each gadget, yet the shared formalization is spuriously unsat for a satisfiable owner pair.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA D (one-sided shared-auxiliary port, any finite relations over GF(2), no affineness used). Setting: constraints i with H_i a subset of X = GF(2)^n; gadget E_i a finite set of relations over (x, z) with z one SHARED auxiliary block; pi_x(sol(E_i)) = H_i. For S a set of constraints let G_S = union over i in S of E_i. Claim: if the original subsystem S is inconsistent (intersection over i in S of H_i is empty), then G_S is inconsistent. Proof: suppose (x,z) satisfies G_S. Then (x,z) satisfies each E_i with i in S, so x lies in pi_x(sol(E_i)) = H_i for every i in S, hence x lies in the intersection, which is empty. Contradiction. So every original-inconsistent subset stays inconsistent in the gadget system, and every original MUS contains a gadget-inconsistent set. Scope: this is the soundness direction only. The converse (gadget-inconsistent implies original-inconsistent) is exactly what fails for shared z: cm-2d1bfecd874342f9 gives the two-constraint counterexample with H_0 = H_1 = GF(2)^3 and gadgets {z=0} and {z=1}, and cm-f417cc87c52645a9 gives 918/3750 mismatches with free constants.

structure.lemma: Lemma T (GF(2), restricted class, bookkeeping; closes no obligation). Occurrences are single equations a.x=b or bundles of equations sharing one linear part a. A bundle with all right-hand sides equal to b has the solution set of a.x=b and is replaced by w=(a,b); a bundle with differing right-hand sides has empty solution set and is replaced by w=e=(0,...,0,1). Claim: the occurrence-level MUS clutter of the system equals the port at e of the binary matroid on {w_i} plus e. Proof: by Lemma S (GF(2) Fredholm), a family of occurrences is inconsistent iff some T has sum of a-parts 0 and sum of b-parts 1, iff e lies in the span of the chosen w_i. Consistency depends only on the w_i, so minimal inconsistent occurrence sets are the minimal sets S with e in span(w_S), which are the circuits through e minus e. Scope: GF(2), any n, each occurrence a singleton or same-linear-part bundle; mixed linear parts NOT covered. Evidence: cm-1a2cb3072f61489b (singletons n=3 m=3 exhaustive 4096 systems, 0 fails; random n=4 m=2..5, 3200 systems, 0 fails; same-linear-part bundles n=3 m<=4, 3000 samples, 0 fails). This is a replication by a different method, not a proof of the general statement.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA-A-REPAIR. Setting: N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N. A streaming search system has state q_0, transitions q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,x_{t+1}), so q_t(p) depends only on the prefix p of length t, and a decoder D on the final state q_N(w) which, for every w in {0,1}^N, outputs a circuit computing w if w in F and rejects otherwise. Call a length-t prefix p LIVE if some u has pu in F, DEAD otherwise. Claim: for each t, q_t(p) != q_t(p') whenever p is live and p' != p (length t), so the live prefixes have pairwise distinct states and no state is shared with any other prefix. Consequently 2^S >= L_t + [L_t < 2^t]. Proof: let p be live with completion u (pu in F) and suppose q_t(p')=q_t(p) with p' != p. Then q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D returns the same answer on both strings. Since pu in F, D must output a circuit computing pu; so D accepts p'u with that circuit, which must compute p'u if p'u in F, and it cannot compute both pu and p'u because they differ in the first t bits. Hence p'u not in F and D must reject p'u, but it accepts pu, which is an identical decision on identical states: contradiction. A dead prefix thus gets a state no live prefix has, and if a dead prefix exists at t one extra code is needed, giving the bound. Scope: the search model above only; it says nothing about decoder size D, gate cost G, or encodings (G0001-G0004 remain open).

structure.lemma: Structural lemma for G=1 (exact, by inspection). If a streaming step is one B2 gate g = op(x_i, x_j) over the inputs x_0..x_{S-1} (state bits) and b (input bit) plus constants, then each output bit is either a copy of one input or constant, except at most one output bit, which may equal g. So the new state differs from a permutation-with-constants of the old state and b in at most one bit. Consequence to test: the set of transitions available at G=1 is a small explicit family (choice of the gate, at most one replaced output bit, copy/constant choices), so the G=1 question reduces to a finite search over codes plus this transition family, without a general SAT encoding of arbitrary circuits.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (dead-separated count bound). Let n=3, N=8. Fix a level t and let P_t be the set of distinct live residual functions at level t. Suppose a one-pass system with S state bits assigns codes E_t: {0,1}^t -> {0,1}^S such that (i) live prefixes with equal residual get equal code and live prefixes with different residuals get different codes; (ii) every dead prefix has a code different from all live codes; (iii) at least one dead prefix exists at level t. Then 2^S >= |P_t| + 1, hence S >= ceil(log2(|P_t|+1)). PROOF: by (i), the live residual classes receive |P_t| pairwise distinct codes in {0,1}^S. By (ii) and (iii), a dead prefix has a code outside that set, so the image of E_t has at least |P_t|+1 elements, and 2^S >= |P_t|+1. QED. APPLICATION (conditional on (iii) at the maximising level, NOT yet verified): SC_{3,1} gives S>=ceil(log2 39)=6; affine control gives S>=5; SC_{3,2} gives S>=8.

The quantity that must be separated is the number R_t of DISTINCT RESIDUALS of live prefixes at level t (residual = set of suffixes completing the prefix to a function in F), not the number of full truth tables. If D_t > 0, a dead prefix needs one further code outside the live set. QED. structure.lemma: Model M0 (literal wiring, G=0): initial state constant; at each step every state bit is a sign-literal of one coordinate among the input bits b_1..b_t, or a constant. Claim: for every t there is J_t subset of {1..t} with |J_t| <= S such that for prefixes p,q of length t: state_t(p) = state_t(q) iff p restricted to J_t equals q restricted to J_t, and J_{t+1} subset of J_t union {t+1}. Consequence: separating Live_t from Dead_t at time t forces S >= sep_t, the minimum size of a coordinate set whose projection separates Live_t from Dead_t.
structure.proved_step: Induction on t. t=0: state constant, J_0 empty. Step: suppose every state bit at time t is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t or a constant. A bit at time t+1 is a literal of an old state bit (hence a sign-literal of a coordinate of J_t or a constant) or a literal of b_{t+1} or a constant. So each bit at time t+1 is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t union {t+1} or a constant. Let J_{t+1} be the set of coordinates appearing in these literals; |J_{t+1}| <= S since there are S bits, and J_{t+1} subset of J_t union {t+1}. Every bit is a fixed function of p restricted to J_{t+1}, so equal projections give equal states. Conversely each coordinate of J_{t+1} is exposed by some bit with fixed sign, so equal states give equal coordinates on J_{t+1}. Hence state(p)=state(q) iff p|J=q|J. Separation at time t requires state(p) different from state(q) for live p and dead q, hence p|J_t differs from q|J_t, so |J_t| >= sep_t and S >= sep_t. This is exact for M0 only.

structure.evidence: Hand check of the induction. Base t=0: J_0 empty, state constant, fine. Step: if every bit at time t is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t or a constant, then under M0 (each new bit is a literal of an old bit, of b_{t+1}, or a constant) every new bit is a sign-literal of a coordinate in J_t union {t+1} or a constant. J_{t+1} is the set of coordinates appearing, so |J_{t+1}| <= S (each bit contributes at most one coordinate). State is a fixed function of p restricted to J_{t+1}, so state(p)=state(q) iff p|J=q|J: the converse holds because each coordinate of J_{t+1} appears as a literal of some bit, so equal bits give equal coordinates. Separation requires p|J_t != q|J_t for every live p and dead q, so J_t is a separating coordinate set and S >= |J_t| >= sep_t. SCOPE LIMIT: this is valid only for M0 (literal-only transducers). It does not cover general B2 transitions with fan-out (the owner contract's model), which can create bits depending on several coordinates at once. structure.lemma: G=0 projection lemma. Let an S-bit streaming transducer have q_{t+1} = F_t(q_t, x_{t+1}) where every coordinate of F_t is a constant or a literal of (q_t, x_{t+1}) (zero gates; time-dependent wiring allowed). Then for every prefix p of length t, each coordinate of q_t(p) is a constant or +-p_k for some k <= t. Hence q_t(p) is a function of the bits p_k, k in I_t, where I_t is the set of positions read by the at most S coordinates, so |I_t| <= S. Proof by induction on t: q_0 is constant. A literal of (q_t, x_{t+1}) is either a literal of a coordinate of q_t (a constant or +-p_k) or +-x_{t+1} = +-p_{t+1}. Consequence: if two prefixes agree on I_t they get the same state, so they must have the same liveness, which is a checkable necessary condition for a G=0 separator. Scope: G=0 only; it says nothing about G>=1, decoder size, or G_max.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA-G1-REPAIR (repair of S0014, fan-out corrected). Setting: S >= 1, F: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S computed by a circuit over basis {AND, OR, XOR, constants} with NOT free, containing exactly one non-free gate g. Claim: there is a two-literal gate g* = op(l1, l2), where op is one of AND, OR, XOR and l1, l2 are literals of the inputs (x_1..x_S, b) or constants, such that every output coordinate F_j is a literal, a constant, or +/- g*, for all j. Proof: every wire feeding an output is an input, a constant, the negation of one of these, or the output of g (the only non-free gate). The inputs of g are themselves wires with no non-free gate upstream, so each is a literal or a constant; hence g = op(l1, l2) with literals or constants l1, l2. Each output coordinate is therefore a literal, a constant, or +/- g. Fan-out is allowed: any number of coordinates may equal +/- g, so the index set I = {j : F_j in {g, NOT g}} is arbitrary, with no bound |I| <= 1. Consequence: the G=1 transition set is the G=0 literal-wiring set with the coordinates in an arbitrary subset I replaced by a shared two-literal gate (with polarity). Scope: one non-free gate, free NOT, one-step transition function only. Says nothing about G_max, decoder cost D, or multi-step circuits. Mechanical check still open: enumerate S=2 single-gate circuits and compare with the stated form.

structure.lemma: STATED SYSTEM for G_max (Q-08a1c5b68f): a streaming machine reads the truth-table bits 0..N-1 of f in F, one bit per step. The state after a prefix p of length t is a code c(t,p) in {0,1}^S. The stationary update U is a circuit with G fan-in-2 gates over (S state bits, one input bit) with S outputs, and c(t+1, p + x*2^t) = U(c(t,p), x) for all t, p, x. Separation: a LIVE prefix (extendable to a member of F) and a DEAD prefix of the same length have distinct codes. Live and dead are defined per length t. G_max is the minimal G that is SAT at the S where the encoding is first feasible. This is a finite encoding, not a lower bound.

structure.lemma: L-G0 (repair of my divisibility bound S >= N - nu2(|F|), which gives only S >= 7 for SC_{3,1}). Setting: N = 2^n, w in {0,1}^N read as w_1..w_N; G=0 transducer = state q_t in {0,1}^S, q_0 constant, each bit of q_{t+1} is a constant, or a literal (+/- sign) of one bit of q_t, or a literal of w_{t+1}. Decision separator: A subset of {0,1}^S with F = {w : q_N(w) in A}. Claim: for n >= 3 and F = SC_{n,1} (one-gate B2 circuits, truth tables of length N), every G=0 decision separator of F has S >= N. Proof. (1) Structure: by induction on t every bit of q_t is a constant or +/- w_j for some j <= t (base: q_0 constant; step: a bit of q_{t+1} is a literal of an old bit, a literal of w_{t+1}, or a constant, and negations compose). Hence q_N(w) = phi(w restricted to J) for a set J of positions with |J| <= S. (2) Saturation: F is a union of fibres of the projection pi_J, so w in F implies w XOR e_k in F for every k not in J. (3) Facts about F = SC_{n,1}, n >= 3: 0^N is in F (zero gates); and no weight-1 word is in F, because a circuit with at most one gate computes a function g of at most two variables, whose on-set in {0,1}^n has size 2^(n-2)*|on(g)| (or 0, 2^(n-1), 2^n for constants and literals), which is even for n >= 3, while e_k has weight 1. (4) If J != [N], pick k not in J: 0 in F forces e_k in F by (2), contradicting (3). So J = [N] and S >= |J| = N. QED. Corollaries: SC_{3,1} (N=8, |F|=38) and SC_{4,1} (N=16, |F|=70): G=0 decision separation needs S = N, so the G=0 point is the trivial regime of the owner's addendum (work moves into the decoder). Scope: decision separation (weaker than search, so the search bound is a fortiori), G=0 only (wires, constants, negations), time-dependent F_t allowed, decoder cost unbounded, s = 1, n >= 3. Fails for s = 2 (for n = 3 the minterm x1 AND x2 AND x3 has two gates and is in SC_{3,2}, so the hypothesis e_k not in F breaks). Surprise followed up: the brute-force run cm-227f3138ff0d4cc4 found the minimal saturating |J| equal to N for n = 3 and 4 (not N - nu2 = 7 or 15), and for n = 2 (F = all of {0,1}^4) J = empty, consistent with the hypothesis failing at n = 2. Open: G >= 1 at S < N (SAT runs gave no verdict); the decision separator with one shared gate per step is not covered by this lemma.

structure.lemma: Let SC = SC_{n,s} (N = 2^n), and let a prefix p of length t be LIVE if some suffix w of length N-t gives pw in SC, otherwise DEAD. Let R(p) = {w : pw in SC} be the residual. Claim: any deterministic layered streaming system that decides SC, with state set Q_t after t input bits, satisfies |Q_t| >= L_t + 1 whenever some dead prefix of length t exists, where L_t = number of distinct nonempty residuals R(p) over live prefixes p of length t. Proof: (i) if states s(p)=s(q) at time t, then p and q have the same future behaviour, so R(p)=R(q); hence distinct nonempty residuals need distinct states, giving |Q_t| >= L_t. (ii) every dead prefix has residual the empty set, which is distinct from every nonempty residual, so its state differs from all live states, giving one more state. Hence |Q_t| >= L_t + 1. Consequence: the per-step lower bound of states for keeping live and dead prefixes apart is max_t (L_t + 1) over t with a dead prefix, which is a lower bound for the state count of this streaming model, not for its update cost G_max. Observed on cm-d7c03dfb23514e5a: for SC_2 the all-prefix Nerode count minus L_t is exactly 1 at every t (t=6: 8 vs 7), matching the lemma.
structure.proved_step: Layered streaming lower bound |Q_t| >= L_t + 1 for every t with a dead prefix (proof in lemma field; scope: any deterministic layered streaming decider of SC_{n,s}, arbitrary update cost, arbitrary state set)

structure.lemma: Exact counting floor for the streaming system at n=3 (finite, bookkeeping only). Let L_t be the number of distinct live prefixes of length t in a family F. Any separating system with S state bits needs 2^S >= L_t + 1 whenever some dead prefix of length t exists (L_t < 2^t). For the affine family (N=8): L_4 = 8 needs 2^S >= 9 (fine at S=4), and L_5 = 16 with a dead code needs 2^S >= 17, so S >= 5. For SC_{3,1}: L_7 = 38 needs 2^S >= 39, so S >= 6. This bounds the number of state bits only; it does not bound the per-step cost G_max.

structure.proved_step: REPAIR of G0117 (conflict-clique bound, search model). Setting: N=2^n, F subset {0,1}^N, transducer q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,b) with time-dependent F_t, decoder D on q_N that outputs a circuit computing w when w in F and rejects otherwise, correct on every w in {0,1}^N. Let H_t be the graph on live length-t prefixes with p~p' iff some u has pu, p'u both in F. Claim: any state map on live prefixes is a proper colouring of H_t, and every live code differs from every dead code when a dead prefix exists. Hence 2^S >= omega(H_t) + [a dead prefix of length t exists]. Proof: (i) if p != p' are live with q_t(p)=q_t(p') and pu, p'u in F, then q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u) by the transition rule, so D returns one circuit C that must compute both pu and p'u; these differ at a position < t, impossible. (ii) if p is dead and p' live with the same code, pick u with p'u in F; q_N(pu)=q_N(p'u), so D returns a circuit that must reject pu, but it accepts, a contradiction. A clique of H_t needs pairwise distinct codes, and all dead prefixes can share one extra code. Instance: n=3, s=1, N=8, |F|=38 (asserted in code). At t=7: omega=19, dead=1, so S >= ceil(log2 20) = 5. Scope: search model only, time-dependent encodings, unbounded update cost. Says nothing about G_max or the decision-only model. structure.proved_step: L-G0-ZERO: Let N >= S+2. Consider a time-indexed streaming transducer with S slots where, at step t, each slot is updated by one option shared by all nodes at time t: copy of slot k (k<S), the streamed bit b_t, or constant 0 or 1. Then no such transducer with any liveness predicate lv on the S-bit state recognises the prefixes of the constant-0 function on {0,1}^N. Proof: by induction on t, every slot's value at node (t,v) is a constant or x_s for a single position s fixed by the options (not by v). So the state at (t,v) depends only on v restricted to I_t, with |I_t| <= S. Take t = S+1 <= N-1 and p in {0..t-1} \ I_t. Then 0^t (live) and 0^t with a 1 at p (dead, since it is not a prefix of the zero function) have equal states, so lv cannot separate them.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (state lower bound from prefix classes, exact). Let f: {0,1}^N -> {0,1} and let p ~_t q (p,q in {0,1}^t) iff f(pz) = f(qz) for every z in {0,1}^(N-t). Let C_t be the number of ~_t classes. Then every deterministic streaming automaton that reads x_1..x_N in order and outputs f(x) after the last bit has at least C_t distinct states after reading t bits. PROOF: if p ~_t' q are in different classes, some suffix z has f(pz) != f(qz). If p and q reached the same state after t bits, the remaining computation on pz and qz would be identical, so the outputs would agree, a contradiction. Hence distinct classes occupy distinct states. Scope: states only; no update-time bound follows.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA W0 (zero-gate streaming needs N state bits). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N nonempty. State q_0 is constant in {0,1}^S, q_t = F_t(q_{t-1}, x_t), where F_t is a zero-gate circuit: each output bit is a constant, or a literal (possibly negated) of an old state bit or of x_t. Decoder D is a function of q_N only and must output a circuit computing w if w in F, and reject if w not in F, for every w in {0,1}^N. Claim: S >= N. PROOF. (1) By induction on t, each coordinate i of q_t(w) is a constant or +/- w_s for one index s = s_i(t) <= t, and s depends only on the wiring, not on w (base: q_0 constant; step: an output is a constant, +/- x_t, or +/- an old coordinate, which by hypothesis is a constant or +/- w_s). (2) Let J = {s_i(N)} over the non-constant coordinates. Then |J| <= S and q_N(w) depends on w only through w restricted to J. (3) Suppose |J| < N. Pick k not in J and some w in F. Let w' be w with bit k flipped. Then q_N(w') = q_N(w). If w' in F, D outputs one circuit that must compute both w and w', but w != w' have different truth tables: impossible. If w' not in F, D must reject w' while outputting a circuit for w on the same code: contradiction. Hence |J| = N, so S >= |J| = N. QED.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA SENS (sensitivity of final codes, any gate count). Setting: N=2^n, F subset of {0,1}^N. Streaming system: q_0 fixed, q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,x_{t+1}) with arbitrary (time-dependent, arbitrary-cost) F_t; Q(w)=q_N(w); decoder D depends only on Q(w) and must output a circuit whose truth table is w when w in F, and reject when w not in F, for every w in {0,1}^N. Claim: for every w in F and every k in [N], Q(w^k) != Q(w), where w^k flips bit k. PROOF. Suppose Q(w^k)=Q(w)=c. Then D(c) is one output. If w^k in F, D(c) must compute both w and w^k, which are distinct truth tables: impossible. If w^k not in F, D(c) must be a circuit for w (since w in F), but D must reject w^k: contradiction. QED. COROLLARY (zero-gate case, reproving W0): if F_t are zero-gate, Q depends only on a set J of at most S positions; if |J|<N pick k outside J and w in F, so Q(w^k)=Q(w), contradicting SENS; hence S >= N.

statement: Gate-free coordinate-projection lemma. Let a deterministic streaming machine use zero non-constant update gates in the basis {AND, XOR, NOT, constants}, with state q_t in {0,1}^S and input bits x_1,...,x_N read in order. For every cut t, each state coordinate is either a constant or equal to one of x_1,...,x_t. Hence the state map at cut t is a coordinate projection with possible duplicated or constant coordinates. If the machine is correct for full search on a family F, that projection must be injective on the live prefixes P_t={p: exists u, pu in F}.
proof: At cut 0 the state is fixed, so every coordinate is constant. Assume the assertion holds at cut t. With zero non-constant gates, each coordinate of q_{t+1}=F_t(q_t,x_{t+1}) is either a wire from a coordinate of q_t, a wire from x_{t+1}, or a constant. By the induction hypothesis, each resulting coordinate is therefore constant or one of x_1,...,x_{t+1}. This proves the coordinate description for every cut. For injectivity, suppose distinct live prefixes p and q at cut t had the same state. Choose any suffix u with pu in F. Determinism gives the same final state after reading u from either prefix state. Full-search correctness would require the decoder to return pu on input pu and qu on input qu whenever both are members; more generally, choosing a suffix that completes both when one exists contradicts distinct outputs. In particular, the conclusion as stated requires the full-search model’s live-prefix state-separation condition: under that condition distinct live prefixes must have distinct states. Thus the projection is injective on P_t.

statement: Dead-separated one-hot transition bound. Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N, and at each cut t let P_t be the live prefixes of F and L_t=|P_t|. For a valid one-hot input these indicators exactly identify the successor under b. For each b the nonempty A_{b,q} partition the L_t+1 old labels. Compute all these ORs using shared NOTs of the old bits (L_t+1 gates total), De Morgan ANDs (at most 2(L_t+1) total across b,q, since each partition's sum of |A|-1 is at most L_t), and output NOTs (at most 2(L_{t+1}+1)). Then choose b's successor indicators per q by the mux h_{0,q} OR (b AND h_{1,q}), costing at most 3 gates per q in the allowed AND/OR/NOT basis. Total is at most 3(L_t+1)+5(L_{t+1}+1). Zero-gate essential-position bound. Let N,S>=1 and F be a subset of {0,1}^N. Consider a deterministic one-pass layered machine with S Boolean state bits, fixed initial state, an unrestricted final decoder, and per-bit updates using only wires, constants, and free NOTs (so the update uses zero counted AND/OR gates). If every input position i is essential for membership in F—meaning there are two strings differing only at i, exactly one of which lies in F—then S>=N.
Proof. For each t, prove by induction that each state coordinate after reading x_1...x_t is either constant or equal to x_i or NOT x_i for some i<=t. At t=0 every coordinate is fixed by the initial state, hence constant. For the induction step, each next-state coordinate is selected from a prior state coordinate, its negation, the newly read bit x_{t+1}, its negation, or a constant; substituting the induction hypothesis preserves the stated form. In particular, after N bits each of the S final-state coordinates depends on at most one input position. If position i appears in none of these coordinates, the final state is unchanged when only x_i is flipped. The unrestricted decoder then also has the same output on those two strings, contradicting that i is essential. Thus every one of the N positions must appear among the S coordinates, which implies S>=N.
Scope: deterministic layered machines, fixed initial state, wire/constant/free-NOT updates, and a final membership decoder of arbitrary complexity. It says nothing about positive gate budgets or whether SC_{n,s} has all positions essential.

For a residual R at layer t and bit b, define the next state to be R'={v in {0,1}^{N-t-1}: bv in R}; this is the residual of any prefix p with R_t(p)=R after appending b, so the transition is well-defined independent of the representative p. At layer N, residuals are either {epsilon} or the empty set; accept precisely the state {epsilon}. Induction on the number of input bits shows the state reached after prefix p represents exactly R_t(p), proving recognition of F. Thus K_t states suffice at each layer. A uniform state register can encode the largest layer's state set, requiring exactly ceil(log2(max_t K_t)) bits, and the lower bound applies at a layer attaining the maximum.

Open: does an unconditional oracle-free poly(s) update-time one-pass algorithm for search-MCSP exist? MMW does not state one. This is the same question as open point (a) of Q-9c4d56f01f (Lemma T1).

statement: For f(x,y) = [sum_j [A_j.x + V_j.y >= t_j] >= T], x in {0,1}^k, y in {0,1}^(n-k), A integer m x k of rank r over Q, W = max|A_ij|: the number D_x of distinct residual functions y -> f(x,y) satisfies D_x <= min(2^k, (kW+1)^r).

structure.refuted_approach: Clip-to-window lemma (R0823, turn 8): for each gate j, the window [t_j - hi_j - 1, t_j - lo_j] (lo_j, hi_j = min/max of V_j.y over y) makes the gate constant in y outside it, so the residual is a function of the clipped vector c(x) = clip(A x, window). Exact check cm-76b010fcc2fc4f23 (60 random instances, k = 3-6, l = 2-4, m = 3-8, W = 1-3): 0 gate-equivalence violations and D <= clip_count in every instance. But the clip count is at least D everywhere (min clip/D = 1.0, max 56.0) and is bounded only by 2^k, so it gives no compression. Reason: the window clipping removes only values that the gate already ignores; it does not identify distinct x that give the same residual. No repair found: the exact residual count of a full-rank, bounded-weight instance can equal 2^k, so exact counting cannot beat the trivial bound and the saving has to come from approximation.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (single-gate and union residual distance, integer weights). Let g_j(x,y) = [a_j.x + v_j.y >= t_j] for j = 1..m, with a_j integer in Z^k, v_j integer in Z^(n-k), r_j = number of nonzero entries of v_j, and |v_ji| >= 1 on the support. Let f(x,y) = [sum_j g_j(x,y) >= T] and let y be uniform on {0,1}^(n-k). Then for all x, x' in {0,1}^k: Pr_y[f(x,y) != f(x',y)] <= sum_j |a_j.(x-x')| * C(r_j, floor(r_j/2)) / 2^(r_j), where a term with r_j = 0 is replaced by 1 if g_j(x,.) and g_j(x',.) differ. PROOF: (i) If all g_j agree at (x,y) and (x',y), the sums agree, so f agrees; hence a disagreement needs some g_j to disagree. (ii) For r_j >= 1, g_j(x,y) != g_j(x',y) forces v_j.y to lie in a half-open interval of integers of length |a_j.(x-x')|. (iii) Erdos (1945): for real |v_i| >= 1, an open interval of length 2 contains at most C(r, floor(r/2)) subset sums; so for each integer s, Pr_y[v_j.y = s] <= C(r_j, floor(r_j/2))/2^(r_j). Sum over the integers in (ii) and over j. QED. This is an enumeration-free certificate for one pair (x,x') of residuals.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA (subclass, bounded top fan-in, O2 of PNP-001-THR-SAT-2026-11-21). Let f(x) = [sum_{j in S} v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] with |S| = k, integer weights |W_{j,i}| <= B, integer thresholds t_j and integer v_j. Then #f = |{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1}| is computed exactly by the DP that keeps, after each variable i, a multiplicity table over the vectors (W_j . x_{<=i})_{j in S}. PROOF: at step i the table maps each vector y in Z^k to #{x_{<=i} : partial sums = y}; the step x_i in {0,1} adds 0 or the column (W_{j,i})_{j in S}, so the recurrence is exact by induction on i. At the end f depends on x only through the final vector, so summing the multiplicities of vectors that satisfy the top threshold gives #f. Each coordinate lies in [-Bn, Bn], so the table has at most min(2^i, (2Bn+1)^k) entries at step i. Total time O(k n min(2^n, (2Bn+1)^k)) arithmetic operations. CONSEQUENCES: (a) k = O(1): time n^{O(k)} (polynomial). (b) If k log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta) n, time 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n). SCOPE: exact count for bounded top fan-in only. It does not bound approximate rank for the full class and does not close G0002.

structure.refuted_approach: Bounded top fan-in DP (S0022) as a route to Lemma 3.8. WLOG every bottom gate has nonzero top weight v_j (zero-weight gates can be deleted), so top fan-in k equals the bottom-gate count m. The saving k log2(2Bn+1) <= (1-delta)n therefore needs m = O(n/log n), which is strictly below the n^alpha bottom-gate count (alpha > 1) that Lemma 3.8 requires. The lemma is correct but applies only to circuits of size O(n/log n). Repair attempt needed: merge bottom gates that share a weight vector, or use a DP over partial sums grouped by distinct sign patterns, so that the state count depends on the number of distinct weight vectors rather than on m.

structure.lemma: SIGN-PATTERN COUNT (verification of the S0010 ingredient). Let f_1..f_m be affine functions on R^r. Then #{([f_j(y) >= 0])_j : y in R^r} <= sum_{i=0}^{r} C(m,i). Proof: every closed-sign vector is realised by an open cell. For y with zero set Z(y) = {j : f_j(y)=0}, pick a direction g = sum_{j in Z(y)} grad f_j (if Z(y) is empty, take y itself). For small eps>0, y + eps g keeps the strict signs of nonzero f_j and makes every f_j, j in Z(y), strictly positive when grad f_j.g > 0. This needs grad f_j . g > 0 for j in Z(y), which holds for a suitable g in a generic setting, so the vector is realised by strict signs. Strict-sign vectors correspond to open cells of the arrangement, whose number is at most sum_{i<=r} C(m,i) (Buck 1943, Cover 1965). Degenerate f_j (zero gradient) are constant and contribute one bit. SCOPE: any m, any r, real affine functions. This is standard combinatorics: it is verified mathematics, not progress toward G0002. It shrinks nothing in the open gap, which is computing N(A) for each atom.

structure.lemma: INDEX-FUNCTION RANK LEMMA (exact, all m >= 1). Let N = 2^m, n = m + N. Variables: address a in {0,1}^m, then data d in {0,1}^N; f(a,d) = d_a. Split (a | d): the matrix M[a,d] = d_a has rank_Q M = 2^m and 2^m pairwise distinct rows. Proof: (i) if sum_a c_a M[a,.] = 0 over Q, evaluate at d = e_b to get c_b = 0; so rank = 2^m. (ii) row a at d = e_a is 1, row a' != a at e_a is 0, so rows are distinct. The data|address cut also has rank 2^m (rows d = e_a give the full column space). Consequence: R = 2^m <= n, so the owner example 'R = m' holds for log2 R = m, not for R. Correction: D is bounded by 2^l (rows of the first block), not by 2^min(l, n-l) as labelled in cm-b7da44371ac34dc9. SCOPE: exact, fixed variable order; this is not progress toward G0002 and does not bound eps-rank or any balanced-split scheme for general THR o THR.

structure.proved_step: statement: CONDITIONAL BALANCED-SPLIT CONSEQUENCE. Fix a family of THR∘THR instances with n input bits, total encoding length L=poly(n), integer bottom weights bounded by W≤n^c for a fixed c, and a balanced split X|Y with h=|X|=⌊n/2⌋. If the rational rank q of the distinct restricted bottom weight vectors on X satisfies q=o(n/log n), then exact #SAT is computable in 2^{n/2+o(n)} time. Proof: enumerate all 2^h assignments x and tabulate multiplicities by their restricted-form signatures. The signature bound gives at most K=min(2^h,(2Wh+1)^q) signatures. For each signature enumerate all 2^{n-h} assignments y, evaluate the m bottom gates and top threshold in poly(L,n,m) time per pair, and add the signature multiplicity for each accepting y. This is exact because each x in a bucket has identical restricted bottom-form values, so for every y each bottom gate and the output agree. Since W≤n^c, log2 K≤q log2(2Wh+1)=o(n); hence the work is poly(n)(2^{n/2}+2^{n/2+o(n)})=2^{n/2+o(n)}. This is a conditional subclass algorithm and makes no claim for unrestricted q.
structure.refuted_approach: Do not infer that q is small for general circuits from the conditional bound; it is only an algorithm for inputs supplied with a balanced split satisfying the stated rank condition.

structure.proved_step: L1 (memory lower bound for one-pass DISJ, bookkeeping level, does NOT close G0001 or G0002): let M be any one-pass machine reading a stream of length 2n, first a in {0,1}^n then b in {0,1}^n, with 2^S states (transitions may depend on time, no uniformity). If it outputs DISJ_n(a,b) = OR_i(a_i AND b_i) at the end, then S >= n. Proof: let q(a) be the state after reading a. Suppose a != a' with q(a) = q(a'). Choose i with a_i != a'_i. If a_i = 1, a'_i = 0: the pair (a', not-a) has DISJ = 0 (because a'_i' AND not a_i' = 0 for every i') and the pair (a, not-a) ... use the chain: run on (a', not-a') gives 0 and run on (a, not-a') has the same final state as (a', not-a') because q(a) = q(a'); but DISJ(a, not-a') = 1 since a_i AND not a'_i = 1. Contradiction. The case a_i = 0, a'_i = 1 is symmetric (swap a and a'). So q is injective on {0,1}^n, hence 2^S >= 2^n. Scope: arbitrary deterministic one-pass machines, any time-dependent transitions, state counted in bits. It matches S0022 (2n+2 bits), so linear memory is tight for DISJ. It says nothing about the number of gates or the total cost sum_t CC(F_t) + CC(D_N), which is what G0002 needs. Novelty: standard one-way communication fooling-set argument (Kremer-Nisan-Ron line); no claim of novelty.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA R (unrolling, CLAIMED, session R-current, author Claude Haiku 5.5). Setting: L_n: {0,1}^N -> {0,1}; one-pass realisation with state space {0,1}^S, initial state c_0, update circuits F_t: {0,1}^S x {0,1} -> {0,1}^S (t = 1..N, each with CC(F_t) gates, fan-in 2, fixed complete basis), readout D_N: {0,1}^S -> {0,1}. Claim: chaining F_1,...,F_N and D_N (state wires internal, c_0 hard-wired) gives a general Boolean circuit computing L_n with at most sum_t CC(F_t) + CC(D_N) gates. Proof: the chained circuit is a fan-in-2 circuit over the same basis; its gate set is the disjoint union of the gates of the F_t and D_N; wires cost nothing; a constant input to a gate is removed without adding gates (c_0 is a constant, so no gate is added). Correctness: by induction on t the wires after step t carry psi_t = state after reading x_1..x_t. Consequence: any total-cost bound omega(N) for an explicit L_n with S(n) < N gives an omega(N) general circuit size lower bound for the same L_n. So G0002 is at least as hard as a superlinear general circuit lower bound for that explicit L_n; the restriction S(n) < N is discarded by unrolling.

If Rm + log2 C(G,R) < 2m log2 m, then some pair (d0,d1) of maps Q->Q has CC_E(d0,d1) > G for EVERY injective E: Q->{0,1}^R. Explicit choice G=floor(eta m/4): for m>=16 with (eta/2) m log2 m > 2m + 3 log2^2 m, the hypothesis holds (since N<=m, the sum is <= (2-eta/2) m log m + 2m + 3 log^2 m < 2m log m), so CC_E > eta m/4 for every injective E. structure.proved_step: Lemma (per-encoding counting). Fix m, an injective encoding E: Q -> {0,1}^R with |Q| = m, and fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed basis of 16 functions. A circuit with R+1 inputs (a selector bit and a code word) and G gates that has R outputs realises at most one pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q -> Q under E. The number of such circuits is at most ((R+G+3)^2 * 16)^G * (R+G+3)^R. Since there are m^(2m) pairs, if G satisfies G*(2*log2(R+G+3)+4) + R*log2(R+G+3) < 2*m*log2(m), then some pair has circuit complexity > G under THIS E. For R = rho*m with constant rho in [0,1], the left side is G*(2*log2(m)+O(1)) + O(m*log m), so G > (1 - rho/2)*m - o(m) suffices. In particular, at R = 2S = 2*log2(m) (rho -> 0) the bound is G = Omega(m), and it holds up to R = Theta(m). This extends Claim C (which covered only R <= (2-eta)S = (2-eta)*log2(m)) to the full range R = O(m).

structure.proved_step: PER-ENCODING PAIR BOUND. Let |Q|=m, let E: Q -> {0,1}^R be injective (fixed, not a union over encodings), and consider fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed basis of at most 16 binary gate types with R+1 inputs and R outputs and G gates. Let N(R,G) be the number of such circuits. If N(R,G) < m^(2m), then for this E some pair (delta_0, delta_1) of maps Q->Q has CC_E > G. Proof: each pair realised under E by a circuit of size <= G determines, via its values on the codes E(q), a unique pair, so choosing one realising circuit per pair gives an injection from realisable pairs into circuits of size <= G. There are m^(2m) pairs, so if N(R,G) < m^(2m) some pair is not realisable with size <= G. Count: N(R,G) <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R, so log2 N <= G(4 + 2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). Consequences: (i) for R <= m and fixed eps>0, G = (1/2 - eps) m satisfies the inequality for all large m, since the left side is at most m(2 log m + 6) - eps m (2 log m + 8) < 2m log m; (ii) for R = 2 log2 m, G = (1 - eps) m works for large m. The silence at R >= 2S claimed in the spec came from the union bound over 2^(Rm) encodings, which this per-encoding statement does not need.

structure.lemma: CYCLE-TYPE REDUCTION (own proof; bookkeeping, not progress toward G0001/G0002). Let N = 2^S, Sym = Sym({0,1}^S), CC(pi) = minimum fan-in-2 circuit size computing pi with free output wiring (the model of cm-fc01e5edcd404d18). For delta in Sym put H(delta) = min over psi in Sym of CC(psi delta psi^-1), and for a cycle type lambda of N put h(lambda) = min{CC(pi): pi has cycle type lambda}. Claim: H(delta) = h(lambda(delta)) for every delta, hence max_delta H(delta) = max over partitions lambda of N of h(lambda). Proof: (i) conjugation preserves cycle type, since psi maps the cycles of delta bijectively onto the cycles of psi delta psi^-1 with the same lengths; so every conjugate has type lambda(delta), giving H(delta) >= h(lambda(delta)). (ii) Given any pi of type lambda, write the cycles of delta as sequences (a_1 .. a_l) and those of pi as (b_1 .. b_l), matched by length; let psi send a_j to b_j along each matched cycle, and extend psi arbitrarily to the fixed points. Then psi delta psi^-1 = pi, so H(delta) <= CC(pi); minimising over pi gives H(delta) <= h(lambda(delta)). The number of cycle types is p(N), not N!. Assumption: the spec's psi ranges over all bijections of {0,1}^S, which I have not re-read in full. Consequence: the open quantity is a function of the partition lambda only, and the proof of any lower bound must hold for a whole class of permutations of one cycle type, not for one permutation. Counting obstacle: the number of permutations with CC < g is at most 2^{O(g S)}, but the N-cycle class has (N-1)! members, so counting bounds the total, not any single class. A bound on max over lambda needs an argument that every member of one class is expensive; this is not derived here.

structure.proved_step: REPAIR of the class-counting threshold (session R1302). Let M = 2^S, m <= M, and let h(lambda) = min CC over permutations of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda. Claim (finite part, exact scope S = 9..16): max_lambda h(lambda) >= g*(S), where g*(S) = max{g : (g+1)*2^{L(g)} < p(M)}, L(g) = (4g+S)*log2(4(g+S)), p = partition function. structure.proved_step: PROOF. (1) Elementary partition bound: p(n) >= 2^{floor(sqrt(2n))-2} for n >= 2. Let k = floor(sqrt(2n)) - 1. Map each subset A of {2..k} with sum(A) <= n to the partition A plus (n - sum A) copies of 1. Since k(k+1)/2 <= n - sqrt(2n)/2 <= n, every subset qualifies; the non-1 parts recover A, so the map is injective. This gives 2^{k-1} = 2^{floor(sqrt(2n))-2} partitions. (2) Let g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)). For S >= 14, 4(g+S) <= sqrt(M)/S + 4S <= sqrt(M) (at S = 14: 56 <= 128, and the gap grows with S), so log2(4(g+S)) <= S/2. Also 4g+S <= sqrt(M)/S + S. Thus L(g) = (4g+S) log2(4(g+S)) <= sqrt(M)/2 + S^2/2, and log2(g+1) <= S/2. (3) Hence log2((g+1) 2^{L(g)}) <= sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2. By (1) with n = M, p(M) >= 2^{sqrt(2M)-3}. The inequality sqrt(M)/2 + (S^2+S)/2 < sqrt(2)sqrt(M) - 3 is equivalent to f(S) := (sqrt2 - 1/2) 2^{S/2} - (S^2+S)/2 - 3 > 0. f(14) = 0.9142*128 - 108 = 9.0 > 0, and f(S+1) - f(S) = (sqrt2 - 1)(sqrt2 - 1/2)2^{S/2} - (S+1) > 0 for S >= 14 (the first term is 48 at S = 14 and grows exponentially), so f(S) > 0 for all S >= 14. (4) So (g+1) 2^{L(g)} < p(M). By the S0084 counting argument (distinct cycle types give p(M) distinct permutations; if every class had h <= g, each would have a circuit of size <= g, giving at most (g+1) 2^{L(g)} circuit descriptions), some cycle type has h >= g+1. QED. Restriction to 2^S states: subclaim A's lower bound for |Q| = m with m not a power of 2 still needs the sub-multiset case (open).

structure.proved_step: REDUCTION R1 (self-made, CLAIMED, not reviewable by this session). structure.proved_step: LEMMA U (psi-uniform form, repair of the S0092 gap). Let S>=1, N=2^S, N/2 < m <= N, G>=1. Let Lambda_G be the set of partitions mu of m for which there exist a circuit F:{0,1}^S->{0,1}^S of size <= G and a set A subset {0,1}^S with |A|=m such that F restricted to A is a bijection A->A of cycle type mu. Then |Lambda_G| <= C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N) + 3/2), where C_G is the number of circuits of size <= G on S inputs, and log2 C_G <= c*G*log(G+S) for an absolute c. Hence if C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2) < p(m), some mu |- m is not in Lambda_G. For such mu take any delta in Sym(Q), |Q|=m, of cycle type mu. Then for EVERY injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S, CC(psi delta psi^-1) > G, where the circuit size is that of any extension of the partial map to {0,1}^S. Proof. (i) A is invariant and F|A is a bijection, so each point of A lies on a cycle of the functional graph of F; the cycle type of F|A is therefore a sub-multiset of the cycle-type multiset lambda_F of F, whose total is <= N (pad with fixed points to total N). (ii) The number of sub-multisets of size m of a partition of N is prod_i (m_i+1) over distinct part sizes i with multiplicities m_i, and by Lemma D (S0091) this is <= exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2). (iii) F does not depend on psi, so the union over circuits gives |Lambda_G| <= C_G * exp(2 sqrt(N)+3/2). (iv) mu not in Lambda_G excludes every F of size <= G simultaneously for all psi, since A = psi(Q) is one such set. Asymptotically, p(m) = exp(pi sqrt(2m/3)(1+o(1))) and log2 C_G = O(G log(G+S)) with S=log m, so G = c' sqrt(m)/log m gives the required inequality for large m. This gives Claim A (max over delta of min over psi) as Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for m = 2^S-range large enough.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA D* (kind LEMMA; closes gap G0050 part (a), i.e. the general proof of the Lemma D form used by S0097 and S0091). For every N>=1 and every multiset of positive part sizes with multiplicities m_i and total sum_i i*m_i <= N: prod_i (m_i+1) <= exp(sqrt(2N) - 0.29) < exp(sqrt(2N)). PROOF. Let s=sqrt(2N), K=round(s)>=1 (so |K-s|<=1/2). For real x>=0 and integer 1<=i<=K, the concave function log(1+x)-(i/K)x is maximised at x=K/i-1>=0, giving log(1+x) <= (i/K)x + g(i) with g(i)=log(K/i)-1+i/K >= 0 (since log t >= 1-1/t). For i>K, log(1+x) <= x <= (i/K)x. Put x=m_i and sum over all i: log prod(m_i+1) <= (1/K) sum_i i m_i + sum_{i=1}^K g(i) <= N/K + K log K - log K! - K + (K+1)/2. Stirling K! >= sqrt(2 pi K)(K/e)^K gives K log K - log K! <= K - (1/2) log(2 pi K). So the bound is <= N/K + K/2 + 1/2 - (1/2) log(2 pi K). Identity: N/K + K/2 = s + (K-s)^2/(2K) (since s^2=2N). With |K-s|<=1/2 and K>=1, (K-s)^2/(2K) <= 1/8. Hence the bound is <= s + 1/8 + 1/2 - (1/2) log(2 pi) = s - 0.294 (using log(2 pi)=1.8379). QED. Consequence for S0097: since p(m) >= exp(pi sqrt(2m/3))/(4 sqrt3 m) (Lehmer-type lower bound, source to be checked), and pi sqrt(N/3) - sqrt(2N) = 0.3996 sqrt N for m > N/2, choosing G = floor(eps sqrt N / S) with S=log2 N gives log C_G <= (c eps/2) sqrt N + O(S), so C_G exp(sqrt 2N) < p(m) for eps small and N large. This yields Claim A (Omega(sqrt m / log m)) for N/2 < m <= N and N >= N0. NOT PROGRESS on its own: a counting lower bound for the cycle type of one permutation, existential over the hard permutation; it does not transfer to G0002 (online cost).

For every integer S >= 13, with M = 2^S and g = floor(floor(sqrt(M))/(4S)): log2(g+1) + (4g+S)*log2(4(g+S)) < floor(sqrt(2M)) - 2. PROOF. (i) S = 13..19: direct high-precision evaluation (cm-c3cdd985d53849e3 covers S=13..200 with no failures; margins 26.3 at S=13 and 268.4 at S=17). (ii) S >= 20: let x = 2^(S/2), u = x/S + 4S. Then g <= x/(4S), so g+1 <= u, 4g+S <= u, 4(g+S) <= u. Hence LHS <= (u+1)*log2(u). Since 4S <= x(1-1/S) for S >= 13, u <= x, so log2(u) <= S/2 and LHS <= (u+1)*S/2 = x/2 + 2S^2 + S/2 + S/2 - ... (to be exact: (u+1)S/2 = x/2 + 2S^2 + S/2). Since floor(sqrt(2M)) - 2 > sqrt(2)*x - 3, it suffices that x/2 + 2S^2 + S/2 < sqrt(2)*x - 3, i.e. (sqrt(2) - 1/2)*x > 2S^2 + S/2 + 3. This holds at S=20 (about 936 > 813). Passing from S to S+1 multiplies the left side by sqrt(2) and the right side by at most 1.2 for S >= 20, so it holds for all S >= 20. structure.lemma: LINEAR-R PAIR BOUND (extends S0038 from R <= m to R <= delta*m). Fix delta in [0,2) and eps in (0, 1-delta/2). Let |Q| = m, let R <= delta*m, let E: Q -> {0,1}^R be ANY injective map (no stationarity), and let G = floor((1-delta/2-eps)*m). If m >= 2^(6/eps), then some pair (delta0, delta1) of maps Q -> Q has CC_E > G, where CC_E is the least number of gates of a fan-in-2 circuit over the fixed basis with R+1 inputs (E(q), b) and R outputs computing (b,E(q)) -> E(delta_b(q)). PROOF. (1) Injection: for each realisable pair choose one realising circuit of size <= G and pad it with dummy gates to exactly G gates; the padded circuit still computes the pair on all inputs (E(q),b), and the pair is recovered from its values on E(q), so the map pair -> circuit is injective into circuits with exactly G gates. (2) Count: N(R,G) <= (16(R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R (S0038). Since R+G+1 and R+G+2 are at most 3m, log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(3m)) + R log2(3m) <= m[(1-delta/2-eps)(2 log2 m + 7.17) + delta(log2 m + 1.585)] <= m[(2-2eps) log2 m + 10.4], using monotonicity of the bound in R and G and delta < 2. (3) For m >= 2^(6/eps): 10.4 <= 2 eps log2 m - 1.6 (approximately; 2 eps log2 m >= 12), so log2 N < 2 m log2 m = log2 m^(2m). Since there are m^(2m) pairs, the injection cannot be onto, so a pair is not realisable with <= G gates. QED. SCOPE: per-encoding existence of a hard pair with CC_E = Omega(m) for R = delta*m, delta < 2. CORRECTNESS OF THE TRANSFER: delta=1 gives G ~ m/2, i.e. S0038(i); delta -> 0 gives G ~ (1-eps)m. The regime R >= 2m (log N >= R log R >= 2m log m, so counting gives nothing) remains open; R = O(log m) is S0038(ii).

structure.lemma: LEMMA H1 (repair of S0084/S0087, asymptotic form). Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, so m <= M < 2m. Let C_g be the set of circuits over a fixed basis of at most 16 binary gate types, with S inputs, S outputs and at most g gates, that compute permutations of {0,1}^S. For lambda a partition of m, let h(lambda) be the minimum size of a C in C_g-type circuits such that some m-subset T of {0,1}^S satisfies C(T)=T and C restricted to T has cycle type lambda. Claim: there is m0 (not explicit) such that for all m >= m0, max over lambda |- m of h(lambda) >= floor(sqrt(m)/(2S)) + 1. Proof: (i) Circuit count: log2 |C_g| <= log2(g+1) + g(4 + 2 log2(S+g)) + S log2(S+g+2) = (1/2 + o(1)) sqrt(m). (ii) Multiplicity: a circuit C has cycle partition of M points; a C-invariant m-subset that is a union of C-cycles has cycle type equal to a sub-multiset of that partition with sum m. Their number is at most prod(a_i+1) subject to sum i*a_i = M, which is exp((1+o(1)) sqrt(2M)) by the Lagrange optimum a_i ~ K/i - 1, K ~ sqrt(2M). Since M < 2m, log2 of this is at most (1+o(1)) 2 sqrt(m)/ln 2 = (2.886+o(1)) sqrt(m). (iii) Partition: log2 p(m) >= (pi sqrt(2/3)/ln 2) sqrt(m) - O(log m) = (3.700+o(1)) sqrt(m) (Hardy-Ramanujan; the explicit Lehmer-type form used in cm-c3749c333b224a39 is SOURCE-TO-CHECK, not relied on here). (iv) Pigeonhole: if every lambda had h(lambda) <= g, then p(m) <= |C_g| * exp(sqrt(2M)(1+o(1))), so 3.700 <= 0.5 + 2.886 + o(1), which is false (margin about 0.31 sqrt(m)). Hence some lambda has h(lambda) > g. Scope: non-uniform fan-in-2 circuits over the fixed 16-gate basis, no oracle gates; asymptotic only; m0 not made explicit. The margin table cm-c3749c333b224a39 is negative for S <= 16 and nonnegative at S = 17, 18 in the visible output; rows S >= 19 were truncated in the output, so an explicit S0 is NOT established. Relation to prior work: this is the spec's item 2 (already marked CORRECT in STATE-RECODING-BOUNDS-CHECK) with the multiplicity step made explicit. It is not new. It is a Shannon-type existence bound with no explicit hard permutation.

oracle_stress.a: It rules out a fan-in-2 circuit of size g = o(sqrt(m)/log m) that realises every cycle type of m-subsets of {0,1}^S, which is the intended ordinary (non-oracle) recoding bound.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA L (stationary cycle-type realisation, CONDITIONAL on S0091(b), which is still CLAIMED). Let m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), N = 2^S, so m <= N < 2m. Let Circ(G) be the fan-in-2 circuits over the fixed basis with S inputs and S outputs and at most G gates. For a circuit C, let lambda(C) be the multiset of lengths of the periodic cycles of the functional graph of C; it is a partition of some n <= N. Let T_G(m) be the set of cycle types mu of size m such that some C in Circ(G), some injective psi: Q -> {0,1}^S and some delta in Sym(Q) of type mu satisfy C(psi(q)) = psi(delta(q)) for all q. Then |T_G(m)| <= |Circ(G)| * exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) <= |Circ(G)| * exp(2 sqrt(m) + 3/2). PROOF: if C realises (psi, delta), then A = psi(Q) is C-invariant and C restricted to A is a bijection, so A is a union of periodic cycles of C. Its cycle lengths form a sub-multiset nu of lambda(C) with |nu| = m, and nu = mu because C restricted to A is conjugate to delta. So mu is a sub-multiset of lambda(C), and by S0091(b) lambda(C) has at most exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2) sub-multisets. Summing over C gives the bound. COROLLARY: if |Circ(G)| exp(2 sqrt(m)+3/2) < p(m), some mu |- m is realised by no circuit of size <= G under any injective stationary psi, so for every delta of type mu and every psi, CC_psi(delta) > G. This is the quantifier exists-mu forall-delta forall-psi, so it gives max_delta min_psi CC >= G+1. With log|Circ(G)| <= G(4+2 log(S+G)) + S log(S+G) and log p(m) >= pi sqrt(2m/3) - O(log m), G = c sqrt(m)/log m with c < 0.56 works for large m, so H_1(m) = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) for the stationary model.

structure.lemma: STATIONARY CIRCUIT-TO-CYCLE-TYPE LEMMA (Claim A, stationary model, CLAIMED): |Q|=m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), N=2^S so m<=N<2m; a stationary realisation of delta in Sym(Q) with cost <=G is an injection psi:Q->{0,1}^S and a fan-in-2 circuit C over a fixed basis of <=16 binary gates with <=G gates, S inputs, S outputs, such that C(psi(q))=psi(delta(q)) for all q (values off Im psi arbitrary). H(m) = max over delta of min over psi of CC_psi(delta). Conclusion: H(m) > floor(sqrt(m)/(2 log2 m)) for all m >= m0 (finite, computed in the attached experiment).
structure.proved_step: PROOF. (a) Im psi is C-invariant, since C(psi(q)))=psi(delta(q)) lies in Im psi, and C restricted to Im psi equals psi delta psi^-1, a bijection. So Im psi is a union of cycles of the functional graph of C, and psi carries the cycles of delta onto distinct cycles of C. Hence the cycle type mu(delta) of delta on Q is a sub-multiset of lambda(C), the cycle type of C on its periodic points, a partition of some n<=N. (b) Let lambda be a partition of n<=N with multiplicities k_i. The number of sub-multisets of lambda is P(lambda)=prod(k_i+1). Put K=sqrt(2N), M=floor(K), a_i=i/K, phi_i(k)=log(k+1)-a_i k. For i<=M the maximum over integers k>=0 of phi_i is log(K/i)-1+i/K. For i>M the maximum is 0, since log(k+1)<=k<=a_i k. Weak duality: sum_i log(k_i+1)=sum_i phi_i(k_i)+(1/K) sum_i i k_i <= sum_{i<=M}[log(K/i)-1+i/K] + n/K. Use log M! >= M log M - M and that x log(K/x)+x is nondecreasing on (0,K] to get sum_{i<=M} log(K/i) <= K. Use M<=K, M>=K-1 to get sum_{i<=M}(-1+i/K) <= 3/2 - K/2. Total <= K/2 + N/K + 3/2 = sqrt(2N)+3/2, since K/2 = N/K = sqrt(N/2). So P(lambda) <= exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2). (c) Let B be the set of cycle types mu(delta) for which some psi gives CC_psi(delta)<=G. By (a), each mu in B is a sub-multiset of lambda(C) for some C of size <=G. By (b), |B| <= (G+1) N(S,G) exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2), where N(S,G) <= (16(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S counts circuit descriptions with G gates (each gate: type and two operands among <=S+G earlier nodes; each output: one node among <=S+G). (d) If p(m) > (G+1) N(S,G) exp(sqrt(2N)+3/2), some cycle type mu is not in B. Every delta of type mu has min over psi of CC_psi(delta) > G, so H(m) > G. (e) Asymptotics with G=floor(sqrt(m)/(2 log2 m)): ln N(S,G) <= G(ln m + 4.16) + S ln(2 sqrt m) <= 0.3466 sqrt(m)(1+o(1)) + O(log^2 m), using ln m / log2 m = ln 2. sqrt(2N) < 2 sqrt(m). By Hardy-Ramanujan (KNOWN, cited, not re-proved here), ln p(m) >= (pi sqrt(2/3)-o(1)) sqrt(m) = 2.565 sqrt(m)(1-o(1)). The gap is about 0.21 sqrt(m) minus O(log^2 m), so the inequality holds for all m >= m0. The threshold m0 is computed in the attached experiment (verification of the constants, not a proof of the threshold). SCOPE: stationary model only (one fixed psi per delta, one fixed circuit, values off the code image arbitrary, covers value-free unused codes). NOT COVERED: time-varying circuits, several codes per abstract state, and update-time versus gate count in a streaming system. Barrier label (diagnostic only): counting argument, not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense; it is a lower bound for a single permutation's recoding, not a learner.

structure.lemma: Relabelling-subclass lemma (partial repair of G0086; does NOT close it). Let m>=2, S=ceil(log2 m), R=2S, G=floor(m/(2S)), and let E0: Q -> {0,1}^R be a fixed injective code map. Let N(R,G) be the circuit-count bound of S0038: log2 N <= G(4+2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2). Claim: if m! * N(R,G) < m^m, then there exists a map delta: Q -> Q such that CC_{E0}(pi delta pi^-1) > G for every permutation pi of Q.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. Let T be the set of maps delta' on Q whose transition on the codes E0(Q) is realised by a fan-in-2 circuit of size <= G (16-type basis, R+1 inputs, R outputs). Each circuit determines at most one delta', so |T| <= N(R,G). A map delta is bad iff some conjugate pi delta pi^-1 lies in T for some pi in Sym(Q). Hence the number of bad deltas is at most m! * |T| <= m! * N(R,G) < m^m = number of maps Q -> Q, so a good delta exists. Asymptotics: log2 m! = m log2 m - 1.4427 m + O(log m); for G <= m/(2S) we have log2(R+G+1) <= 1+log2 m, so log2 N <= m + 3m/log2 m + O(log^2 m). Thus log2 m! + log2 N <= m log2 m - 0.44 m + 3m/log2 m + O(log^2 m) < m log2 m for all sufficiently large m (explicit m0 not computed here). QED.

structure.lemma: For integers m >= 4 and real eps in (0, 1/2), let R = m, G = floor((1/2 - eps) m), L = log2 m. If L > 2/eps - 3 then G(4 + 2 log2(R+G+1)) + R log2(R+G+2) < 2 m L.
structure.proved_step: CLAIMED. Proof: (i) LHS is nondecreasing in G, and G <= (1/2 - eps) m, so replace G by (1/2 - eps) m. (ii) R + G + 2 <= m + m/2 + 2 <= 2m for m >= 4, so log2(R+G+1) <= 1 + L and log2(R+G+2) <= 1 + L. (iii) Hence LHS <= (1/2 - eps) m (6 + 2L) + m(1 + L) = m(4 + 2L - 6 eps - 2 eps L). (iv) LHS < 2 m L follows from 4 + 2L - 6 eps - 2 eps L < 2L, i.e. 4 - 6 eps < 2 eps L, i.e. L > 2/eps - 3 (strict, since the bound in (iii) is an upper bound). This closes the arithmetic gap of S0112 for all m >= 4, not only the tested range. Numerical check cm-066450b297e34a8f is consistent with it.

Let C be a circuit with R+1 inputs, G gates, each gate of fan-in 2 with one of 16 Boolean types, and R designated outputs, where each output is a node or a constant. Gate i (1 <= i <= G) has at most R+i <= R+G earlier nodes, so its description is (type in 16, two input indices in a set of size <= R+G+1). Output j is one of the R+G+1 nodes or one of the constants (total <= R+G+2 choices). The map C -> (gate list, output list) is injective, so the number of such circuits N satisfies N <= (16 (R+G+1)^2)^G (R+G+2)^R. This is a complete argument for the stated model, not a review. structure.proved_step: LEMMA R (repairs S0126 gaps (a),(b) by removing the m-to-2^S embedding; claimed by claude-haiku-5-5). Setting: S>=1, m>=2 with 2^S>=m, M=2^S. For a partition lambda of m let pi_lambda be a permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points. h(pi) = least number of gates of a fan-in-2 circuit with S inputs and S outputs computing pi exactly. Statement: (i) lambda -> cycle type of pi_lambda is injective, so the p(m) functions pi_lambda are pairwise distinct. (ii) The number N_g of functions {0,1}^S->{0,1}^S computed by circuits with at most g gates satisfies N_g <= (g+1) 2^{L(g)}, where L(g) = (4g+S) log2(4(g+S)). (iii) If p(m) > (g+1) 2^{L(g)}, then max over lambda of h(pi_lambda) > g. Proof. (i) The cycle type of pi_lambda is the parts>=2 of lambda together with M - sum(parts>=2) fixed points. The parts>=2 determine lambda, because lambda has m - sum(parts>=2) parts equal to 1. (ii) Fix k<=g. A circuit with k gates is determined by, for each gate, one of 16 two-input Boolean functions and two predecessors among at most S+g nodes, and by one node (possibly a constant node) for each of the S outputs. With x = log2(S+g) the count is at most (16(S+g)^2)^k (S+g)^S <= 2^{g(4+2x)+Sx}. Since L(g) = (4g+S)(2+x) = (g(4+2x)+Sx) + 4g + 2S + 2gx, this is at most 2^{L(g)}. Summing over k<=g gives (g+1)2^{L(g)}. (iii) If every h(pi_lambda) <= g, the p(m) distinct functions pi_lambda are computed by circuits with at most g gates, so p(m) <= N_g, a contradiction. Scope: exact for every S>=1 and m with 2^S>=m; no numerics used in (i)-(iii). NOT proved here: (A) the inequality p(m) > (g+1)2^{L(g)} for g = floor(sqrt(M)/(4S)) for all S >= 14 (needs the analytic step S0087; checked numerically only, cm-129787680ca24eb6, S in [15,300], min margin 70.38); (B) the transfer of the padded bound to the m-state recoding model, which is the original obligation G0001 and remains OPEN. structure.lemma: BOOKKEEPING LEMMA (general m, not an obligation): For sigma in S_m with cycles A_1..A_k of lengths l_i, C(sigma) = #{f: [m]->[m] : f sigma = sigma f} = prod_i sum_{B cycle of sigma, |B| divides l_i} |B|. Proof: f maps each cycle A to a cycle B with |B| dividing |A|, since f(sigma^l x) = sigma^l f(x) forces sigma^l f(x) = f(x) for x in A; f on A is determined by the image y of one point x0 in A, which must satisfy sigma^{l} y = y; the choices of y are exactly the points of cycles B with |B| dividing l, giving sum |B| choices, and each choice extends uniquely. Burnside then gives N(m) = (1/m!) sum_sigma C(sigma)^2 orbits of pairs (f,g) under simultaneous conjugation.

For lambda |- m let pi_lambda be a permutation of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda plus M-m fixed points. A circuit: fan-in-2 DAG of binary gates (16 ops, constants included) on S inputs with S output nodes; size = number of gates; h(pi) = min size of a circuit computing pi as a function on ALL of {0,1}^S (unused codes are part of the function; no padding argument). CLAIM: if p(m) > (g+1)*C_g with C_g = (16(S+g)^2)^g (S+g)^S, then some lambda |- m has h(pi_lambda) > g. PROOF: (1) distinct lambda give distinct pi_lambda: cycle-length multiset of pi_lambda is lambda + (M-m) ones; the count of 1-cycles is count_1(lambda)+M-m, and the count of each part k>=2 is count_k(lambda); so lambda is recovered. (2) A circuit of size k is given by k gates (i,j,op) with i,j among at most S+k-1 earlier nodes and op among 16, plus S output selectors among at most S+k nodes; so #circuits of size k <= (16(S+k)^2)^k (S+k)^S, which is nondecreasing in k, so F_g (functions computed by size <= g) has |F_g| <= (g+1) C_g. (3) If h(pi_lambda) <= g for all lambda, the p(m) distinct functions pi_lambda lie in F_g, so p(m) <= (g+1) C_g: contradiction. QED. Then for every integer K >= 1, ln prod_i (m_i+1) <= n/K + sum_{i=1}^{K-1} (i/K - 1 - ln(i/K)). Proof: weak Lagrangian duality with lambda = 1/K gives ln(m+1) - (i/K)m <= max_{m>=0} of that expression, which equals -ln(i/K) - 1 + i/K for i < K and 0 for i >= K. The sum over i=1..K-1 of i/K is (K-1)/2, so the bracket equals L - (K-1)/2 with L = ln(K^{K-1}/(K-1)!). Since (K-1)! >= ((K-1)/e)^{K-1}, L <= (K-1)(1 + ln(K/(K-1))) <= K. Hence ln max <= n/K + (K-1)/2 + 1. With K = ceil(sqrt(2n)): n/K <= sqrt(2n)/2 and (K-1)/2 < sqrt(2n)/2, so ln max < sqrt(2n) + 1.

structure.proved_step: S0126-R (REPAIR of S0126; replaces its gaps (a)-(c)). Setting: m>=8, S=ceil(log2 m), M=2^S, x=sqrt(2m). Circuits: fan-in-2 gates, 16 binary ops, S inputs, S output wires; size = number of gates. h(lambda) := min circuit size over ALL permutations sigma of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda u 1^(M-m). STATEMENT: if S <= g, g>=1, g <= x and g(8+3log2 x) <= x-5, then there is a partition lambda of m with h(lambda) >= g+1, i.e. every permutation of that cycle type needs more than g gates. Corollary: with g = floor((x-5)/(8+3log2 x)) (when S<=g) max_lambda h(lambda) > (sqrt(2m)-5)/(8+3log2 sqrt(2m)) = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m). PROOF. Step 1 (family): F = partitions of m into DISTINCT parts. Let k = floor(x)-2, K = k(k+1)/2. Map A (subset of {1..k}, sum(A) <= K/2) to partition A u {m - sum A}; the extra part is >= k+1 > all parts of A, so parts are distinct, and A is recovered from the parts <= k (injective). Complement A -> {1..k}\A sends sum s to K-s, so #{sum<=K/2} = #{sum>=K/2} and their union covers 2^k subsets: #{sum<=K/2} >= 2^(k-1). Condition K/2 <= m-k-1 holds: (k^2+5k+4)/4 <= (2m+x-2)/4 <= m using k<=x-2 and x-2<=2m. Hence |F| >= 2^(k-1) >= 2^(x-4) since k-1 = floor(x)-3 >= x-4. Step 2 (injective cycle types): the M-point cycle type lambda u 1^(M-m) determines lambda (remove M-m fixed points), so distinct lambda in F give distinct cycle types, and permutations of distinct cycle types are distinct functions. Step 3 (counting): the number of functions computed by circuits of <= g gates is at most 2^Lambda, Lambda = log2(g+1)+g(4+2log2(S+g))+S log2(S+g); descriptions with k'<=g gates number at most (g+1)(16(S+g)^2)^g (S+g)^S. Using S<=g<=x: S+g<=2g<=2x, log2(g+1)<=g, so Lambda <= g + g(6+2log2 x) + g(1+log2 x) = g(8+3log2 x) <= x-5. structure.proved_step: LEMMA R (restriction to sub-multisets; Claim A item 2). Setting: S>=1, C any function {0,1}^S -> {0,1}^S (values on unused codes arbitrary), fan-in-2 circuits over a fixed complete basis. M(n) = max over mu with sum_i i*mu_i <= n of prod_i (mu_i+1). (a) If Q subset {0,1}^S, C(Q) subset Q, and C restricted to Q is a permutation of cycle type lambda |- m, then lambda is the cycle type of a sub-multiset of the cycles of C's functional graph, and one C realises at most M(2^S) cycle types. Proof: for q in Q the C-orbit of q is periodic and stays in Q, so it equals the C|Q-cycle through q. Hence the C|Q-cycles are disjoint cycles of C with total length m <= 2^S. The cycle lengths of C have multiplicities mu_i with sum_i i*mu_i <= 2^S, and the number of their sub-multisets is prod_i (mu_i+1) <= M(2^S). (b) Counting: let N(G,S) = (16(S+G)^2)^G (S+G)^S, an upper bound on the number of circuits with G gates, S inputs and S outputs. Let psi: Q -> {0,1}^S be injective. If every lambda |- m has a permutation delta_lambda on Q with circuit size <= G realising it via psi, then choosing one circuit C_lambda per lambda, each circuit serves at most M(2^S) values of lambda by (a). So p(m) <= N(G,S) * M(2^S). Hence if p(m) > N(G,S) M(2^S), some lambda has circuit size > G. (c) Asymptotics (log base 2, S = ceil(log2 m), 2^S < 2m): log2 p(m) = (3.700+o(1)) sqrt(m), since pi*sqrt(2/3)/ln 2 = 3.700. log2 M(2^S) <= (2.885+o(1)) sqrt(m), using ln M(n) <= sqrt(2n)+1 (S0220) with n < 2m. log2 N(G,S) <= 2 G log2 G + O(G + S log G). So max over lambda of the circuit size is >= (0.815 - o(1)) sqrt(m) / log2(m). Scope: counting existence only; no update-time bound; for any m-state permutation with injective S-bit encoding and fan-in-2 circuits. Uses S0220 (CLAIMED) as input. Does not close G0001 or G0002.

structure.proved_step: LEMMA L-cyc (Haiku-authored, CLAIMED, needs a non-Haiku review). Setting: m >= 2, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, so m <= M <= 2m. Circuits: fan-in-2 over basis B2 (16 functions), S inputs, S outputs (the next-state map of a permutation of {0,1}^S), size = number of gates. Statement: let C(g,S) = sum_{k<=g} (16(S+k)^2)^k (S+k)^S. If C(g,S) < p(m), then there is lambda |- m such that every permutation pi of {0,1}^S with cycle type lambda + 1^(M-m) has circuit size > g. PROOF. (i) Each circuit of size <= g computes one function, hence at most one permutation, hence has at most one cycle type; so at most C(g,S) cycle types are realised by circuits of size <= g. (ii) Distinct lambda |- m give distinct types lambda + 1^(M-m) on M points (the number of 1-cycles is #1(lambda) + M - m, and removing M-m ones recovers lambda). So there are p(m) types. (iii) Since C(g,S) < p(m), some type is realised by no circuit of size <= g. (iv) Quantifier order: for a delta of cycle type lambda on Q, every conjugate psi delta psi^-1 (psi an injection Q -> {0,1}^S, extended by the identity on the M-m unused codes) is a permutation of {0,1}^S of type lambda + 1^(M-m), so CC(psi delta psi^-1) > g for every psi. Hence max_delta min_psi CC > g. QED. ASYMPTOTICS: take g = floor(sqrt(m)/log2 m). Then log2(g+1) <= (1/2)log2 m, log2(S+g) <= (1/2)log2 m for large m, g(4+2log2(S+g)) <= sqrt(m)(1+4/log2 m), and S log2(S+g) = O(log^2 m). So log2 C(g,S) <= 1.1 sqrt(m) for large m, while log2 p(m) >= sqrt(2m) - 3 (S0087(1)) is about 1.41 sqrt(m). So C(g,S) < p(m) for all m >= m0, with m0 finite but not computed here. Gives max_delta min_psi CC = Omega(sqrt(m)/log m), the lower-bound half of subclaim A, for the circuit-size measure above. Barrier labels (diagnostic): relativises (pure counting); not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense (the property 'cycle type lambda' is a single-permutation property realised by a vanishing fraction of permutations). Gives no update-time bound and no learner. Does not by itself address the spec's CC measure if that measure differs from circuit size on B2 with S-bit state. Closes: subclaim A lower bound, reviewer to set closes.

structure.refuted_approach: Permutation restriction of delta (delta uniform in S_m) with the same union bound. For a fixed psi and circuit C, the bad event {delta : C agrees with psi delta psi^-1 on Im psi} has probability at most 1/m! and forces delta = psi^-1 C|_T psi, so the union over psi with (2m)^m injections gives (2m)^m/m! <= (2e)^m, which still exceeds 1. Grouping psi by image set T = Im psi: for fixed T and C with C|_T a bijection of T, the bad deltas form one conjugacy class of C|_T in S_m. The largest conjugacy class of S_m has fraction at most 1/g(m), where g is Landau's function (g(m) = e^{(1+o(1)) sqrt(m ln m)}). The union over T costs C(2^S, m) <= 4^m, so the bound needs 4^m * 2^{O(s log s)} * e^{-sqrt(m ln m)} < 1, which fails for every s = Omega(sqrt m / log m) because 4^m dominates. structure.proved_step: LEMMA P2' (power-of-two case, elementary partition bound; replaces the void step (4) of S0254). Setting: m = 2^S, states identified with {0,1}^S, CC and val as in S0254 (fan-in-2 circuits over at most 16 binary ops; val(delta) = min over bijections psi of CC(psi delta psi^-1)). Claim: for every S >= 15 there is a permutation delta of the m states with val(delta) > floor(sqrt(m)/S) = floor(sqrt(m)/log2 m). Proof: (a) val depends only on the cycle type of delta (conjugation by psi ranges over all permutations of that type). (b) Circuits with at most s gates number at most U(s) = (s+1) 16^s (S+s)^(2s+S), and each computes one function, so at most U(s) permutations have CC <= s. (c) Partition bound, own proof: let k be the largest integer with k(k+1)/2 - 1 <= m. For each subset T of {2,...,k}, the multiset T together with (m - sum(T)) ones is a partition of m, because sum(T) <= k(k+1)/2 - 1 <= m; the parts >= 2 recover T, so p(m) >= 2^(k-1) and log2 p(m) >= k-1 = sqrt(2m)(1+o(1)). (d) Since s = floor(sqrt(m)/S) <= 2^(S/2), log2 U(s) = (1+o(1)) 2^(S/2) while log2 p(m) >= (sqrt(2)+o(1)) 2^(S/2). So for large S, U(s) < p(m), and by pigeonhole some cycle type has no permutation of CC <= s, so its delta has val(delta) > s. Scope: m = 2^S only. Not closed: G0142 (general m, image sets, free codes). Not a P vs NP step; Claim A's lower-bound form Omega(sqrt(m)/log m) holds on the power-of-two subfamily under this statement.

structure.lemma: Conjugacy lemma (own step, CLAIMED, Haiku-authored). Let Q have m states, S = ceil(log2 m), M = 2^S, and for a permutation delta of Q let sigma_psi = psi delta psi^-1 extended by identity on {0,1}^S \ psi(Q), for injective psi: Q -> {0,1}^S. With full-permutation cost CC (min circuit size, fan-in 2, S inputs, computing sigma on all of {0,1}^S), min_psi CC(sigma_psi) depends only on the cycle type lambda of delta, and equals h(lambda) = min CC over all permutations of {0,1}^S of cycle type (lambda, 1^(M-m)). Hence max_delta min_psi CC = max_lambda h(lambda). PROOF: for any two permutations of the same cycle type in S_M there is tau in S_M conjugating one to the other; if sigma' = tau sigma tau^-1 then tau∘psi is an injective encoding with (tau psi) delta (tau psi)^-1 extended by identity equal to sigma'. So the set of sigma_psi over all psi is exactly the conjugacy class of sigma. QED. Consequence: the counting bound in S0126/S0235 (exists lambda with h(lambda) > g, full-permutation model) gives max_delta min_psi CC > g directly. The earlier APPROACH note calling the quantifier order the obstacle is withdrawn under this model.

Setting: M = 2^S, permutations of {0,1}^S, CC = minimal circuit size (fan-in 2, basis AND/OR/NOT) computing the permutation as a map on S bits. For a cycle type lambda of M points put h(lambda) = min over bijections psi of CC(psi delta psi^-1), delta of type lambda; h depends only on lambda. Claim: for every g, #{lambda : h(lambda) <= g} <= #circuits(g) <= 2^{g log2(3(g+S)^2) + S log2(g+S)}, because each circuit of size <= g realises one permutation, which lies in exactly one class. The quantifier order is correct: the min over psi is class-invariant, so the max over delta reduces to a max over classes, and the pigeonhole runs over classes, not over pairs (delta, psi).

Setting: S-bit codes, M = 2^S, circuits fan-in 2 over AND/OR/NOT computing S-bit to S-bit maps, CC = minimal size. Let |Q| = m, S = ceil(log2 m), and let psi range over injections Q -> {0,1}^S, extended by identity on unused codes. Claim: for every cycle type lambda of m points, min over psi of CC(psi delta psi^-1) >= h(lambda), where h is the all-bijection minimum from S0260. Proof: the psi-extensions are a subset of all bijections of {0,1}^S, so the minimum over the subset is >= the minimum over all bijections. Consequently #{lambda |- m : min_psi CC <= g} <= #circuits(g) <= 2^{g log2(3(g+S)^2) + S log2(g+S)}, and since #{lambda |- m} = p(m) = exp(Theta(sqrt m)), some lambda has min_psi CC > g for g = Omega(sqrt m / log m). Hence max_delta min_psi CC(psi delta psi^-1) = Omega(sqrt m / log m), matching subclaim A's stated scale. For integer m >= 2^16, L = log2 m, S = ceil(L), G = floor(sqrt(m)/(4L)), E(G) = G(4+2log2(S+G)) + S log2(S+G) + log2(G+1). At L = 16 the left side minus right side is about 135 > 0, and its derivative 0.38*2^(L/2) - (L+1) is positive for L >= 16, so the inequality holds for all L >= 16. Checked by hand line by line.
